correctness.rationale: Minimizing f-lambda² as a quadratic in t=x²≥0 reduces its global nonnegativity to gamma1+gamma2*y ≤ sqrt(2lambda+y²)+y for all y≥0; negative y is weaker by absolute values. The normalized strictly convex supporting curve h(z)=(z+sqrt(z²+2))/sqrt(2) has derivative range [1/sqrt(2),sqrt(2)); its supporting-line infimum is 1 when gamma2≤1 and sqrt(gamma2(2-gamma2)) for 1<gamma2<2. Tangency at positive y when gamma2>1 creates nonzero co-minimizers exactly at equality, while equality for gamma2≤1 occurs only at origin. If gamma2≥2, positive gamma1 prevents minimality. Nine rational exact tangency cases checked independently; infinite inequalities rest on convexity, not grid tests.
residual_risks: Only the 2-variable n=3 case and positive parameters; no higher-dimensional chain claim.
